routes: admin.js (Admin CRUD, Bulk upload, Quality sync)
test.js (Main test engine, Atomic sessions, Submit logic)
workers: emailWorker.js (BullMQ processor, DLQ via file log)

duplicate_logic: api.js fetches directly from DB then falls back to JSON, while test.js does the same logic but wraps it in SingleFlight promises.
test.js submission re-fetches questions (DB then JSON fallback) to validate answers. This logic is partially duplicated in getAvailableQuestions elsewhere.
circular_dependencies_potential: adaptiveLearningService requires QuestionSelectionService, and QuestionSelectionService might need adaptive logic in some contexts (though currently injected from route).
frontend_runtime_risks: Event listeners are bound directly on elements (`addEventListener`), potential for listener stacking if panels re-render without cleanup.
innerHTML is used extensively (`grid.innerHTML = ...`), destroying old DOM and listeners, which mitigates stacking but risks memory leaks if references are kept.
Timer management uses a global `timerInterval`. `clearInterval` is called, but race conditions during rapid navigation could cause dangling intervals.
stale_state_risks: admin.js triggers `syncToJSON` asynchronously (`syncToJSON(subject).catch(...)`) without waiting. This can cause the JSON to lag behind MongoDB.
TestSession relies on frontend sending `answers` array in exact index order. If the frontend reshuffles or skips an index unexpectedly, backend score validation breaks.
security_risks: Auth password reset token is hashed correctly (Phase 8), but rate limiting is only on `/api/questions`, not explicitly on login or forgot-password (unless handled in app.js globally).
cache_risks: cache.js falls back to local Map. In a multi-node deployment, this means local caches will drift significantly from Redis and each other.
